evidence: Mara said, 'I guarantee the specimen plates by Monday.'
I will send you the annotated lichen atlas plates on Thursday.
examples.rationale: The meeting quotation is reported, but the field editor separately makes an unconditional future delivery assertion.
examples.text: At the meeting, Mara said, 'I guarantee the specimen plates by Monday.' My commitment is separate: I will send you the annotated lichen atlas plates on Thursday.

evidence: 'You will have the specimen plates before the exhibition,' Mara assured us
examples.rationale: The assurance belongs to a colleague in a recalled meeting. The author does not adopt it as a new delivery commitment.
examples.text: 'You will have the specimen plates before the exhibition,' Mara assured us during Tuesday's meeting. That is the assurance I recorded in my field-editor notes.

evidence: you will receive the numbered lichen plates from my team tomorrow
I am confirming our delivery here
examples.rationale: The author explicitly confirms future recipient receipt from their team. The later meeting recollection does not change that attribution.
examples.text: For the atlas handover, you will receive the numbered lichen plates from my team tomorrow. Someone used nearly those words in the meeting, but I am confirming our delivery here.

evidence: I remember telling the meeting, 'I will deliver the lichen specimen plates on Friday.'
That recollection records what I said last month
examples.rationale: A recalled first-person promise remains reported speech. The author expressly frames it as a historical record rather than a renewed commitment.
examples.text: I remember telling the meeting, 'I will deliver the lichen specimen plates on Friday.' That recollection records what I said last month; it does not renew the commitment.

evidence: Yesterday we finished the marionette rigging
we will send you its revised diagrams tomorrow
examples.rationale: Completed physical work is followed by a distinct, unconditional promise to deliver the diagrams.
examples.text: Yesterday we finished the marionette rigging; we will send you its revised diagrams tomorrow.

evidence: Please send the marionette rigging diagrams to the rehearsal desk
Our crew finished hanging the control bars this morning.
examples.rationale: The only future delivery sought is an action requested from the recipient. The author's crew action is completed past work.
examples.text: Please send the marionette rigging diagrams to the rehearsal desk before lunch. Our crew finished hanging the control bars this morning.

evidence: The marionette lines are installed, and the rigging diagrams were delivered to the stage office yesterday.
examples.rationale: Both the rigging status and diagram delivery concern completed work, with no future delivery assertion.
examples.text: The marionette lines are installed, and the rigging diagrams were delivered to the stage office yesterday.

evidence: Could you reserve a table for the diagram review?
I will be handing over the final marionette rigging diagrams at ten tomorrow.
examples.rationale: The opening request is separate from the author's scheduled future-progressive delivery. That concrete handover is unqualified.
examples.text: Could you reserve a table for the diagram review? The puppet bridge is already rigged. I will be handing over the final marionette rigging diagrams at ten tomorrow.

evidence: You will receive our canal-lock inspection folio before the lock reopens.
examples.rationale: The author assures recipient receipt. Reopening supplies a deadline, not a delivery dependency.
examples.text: You will receive our canal-lock inspection folio before the lock reopens.

evidence: We will deliver the inspection folio when the lower chamber has been drained.
examples.rationale: Delivery depends on draining the chamber. Definite future wording does not remove the stated dependency.
examples.text: We will deliver the inspection folio when the lower chamber has been drained. The submerged masonry photographs are still missing.

evidence: Before the reopening ceremony, I will place the bound canal-lock inspection folio in your hands.
That handover does not depend on the chamber-draining schedule.
examples.rationale: The author directly commits to a concrete handover before an event and explicitly excludes the possible draining dependency.
examples.text: Before the reopening ceremony, I will place the bound canal-lock inspection folio in your hands. That handover does not depend on the chamber-draining schedule.

evidence: If the chamber is drained by Wednesday, you will have the completed inspection folio before reopening.
examples.rationale: The receipt assurance is scoped by an explicit condition. The reopening deadline does not make it unconditional.
examples.text: If the chamber is drained by Wednesday, you will have the completed inspection folio before reopening.

evidence: Neri promised, 'I will dispatch the meteorite custody cards tomorrow.'
examples.rationale: The registrar reports a colleague's promise without making a delivery assertion of their own.
examples.text: Neri promised, 'I will dispatch the meteorite custody cards tomorrow.' I have entered that statement in the collection log.

evidence: I will not dispatch the meteorite custody cards on Friday or later.
examples.rationale: The future dispatch is explicitly negated. Describing the cards as drafts does not assert another delivery.
examples.text: I will not dispatch the meteorite custody cards on Friday or later. These are internal draft records.

evidence: Neri's earlier promise covered the labels.
I guarantee that I will deliver the meteorite custody cards to you tomorrow.
examples.rationale: The colleague's historical promise is distinct from the registrar's explicit, unconditional guarantee of card delivery.
examples.text: Neri's earlier promise covered the labels. As registrar, I guarantee that I will deliver the meteorite custody cards to you tomorrow.

evidence: I will not send the obsolete custody-card set
I will send you the corrected meteorite custody cards at nine tomorrow
examples.rationale: Negation applies only to the obsolete set. The corrected cards have a separate affirmative, unconditional future dispatch assertion.
examples.text: I will not send the obsolete custody-card set; I will send you the corrected meteorite custody cards at nine tomorrow.

evidence: Friday was only a target for delivering the Braille score proofs.
We will deliver them on Friday; we will do so.
examples.rationale: The author explicitly replaces the earlier tentative schedule with an unqualified final assurance.
examples.text: Friday was only a target for delivering the Braille score proofs. I am making it a commitment now. We will deliver them on Friday; we will do so.

evidence: We expect to send the Braille score proofs on Friday, provided the source score arrives on Wednesday.
examples.rationale: Delivery is both an expectation and dependent on receipt of the source score. The dependency is never resolved.
examples.text: We expect to send the Braille score proofs on Friday, provided the source score arrives on Wednesday. That dependency remains open.

evidence: Our working plan had been to share the Braille score proofs sometime next week
I can promise you that I will send the complete proof file on Monday
examples.rationale: The later explicit can-promise assurance supersedes the earlier plan and commits to delivery of a concrete document.
examples.text: Our working plan had been to share the Braille score proofs sometime next week, but I can promise you that I will send the complete proof file on Monday.

evidence: We will deliver the Braille score proofs on Friday unless the source score is late.
Friday delivery is guaranteed.
The source-score exception still applies.
examples.rationale: The passage alternates between a conditional delivery and an unqualified guarantee, then reaffirms the exception. It does not clearly establish whether the guarantee overrides the dependency or is itself conditional, so it is retained outside binary scoring.
examples.text: We will deliver the Braille score proofs on Friday unless the source score is late. Friday delivery is guaranteed. The source-score exception still applies.

evidence: With a second survey boat, we would deliver the salt-marsh transect overlays by Thursday.
examples.rationale: The delivery is hypothetical and depends on an unavailable resource. It is not a direct future commitment.
examples.text: With a second survey boat, we would deliver the salt-marsh transect overlays by Thursday. We have only one boat assigned.

evidence: Our team can export and send salt-marsh transect overlays in either of those formats.
examples.rationale: The author describes capability without committing to a future delivery.
examples.text: Our team can export and send salt-marsh transect overlays in either of those formats.

evidence: I can promise that our team will deliver the salt-marsh transect overlays by Thursday.
examples.rationale: Can promise introduces an explicit assurance, rather than merely describing export or delivery capability.
examples.text: I can promise that our team will deliver the salt-marsh transect overlays by Thursday.

evidence: A finer grid would make hypothetical overlays easier to compare.
For the existing survey, you will receive the completed transect overlays from us tomorrow.
examples.rationale: The hypothetical design observation is separate from an assured future receipt of the existing survey's concrete overlays.
examples.text: A finer grid would make hypothetical overlays easier to compare. For the existing survey, you will receive the completed transect overlays from us tomorrow.

evidence: Please unlock the heritage tram depot office at eight.
We finished the winding trials yesterday, and I will hand you the revised winding schedules at eight fifteen.
examples.rationale: The request and completed trials do not qualify the distinct, unconditional schedule handover.
examples.text: Please unlock the heritage tram depot office at eight. We finished the winding trials yesterday, and I will hand you the revised winding schedules at eight fifteen.

evidence: The workshop completed the winding trials yesterday.
Would you send the updated winding schedules to the heritage tram depot?
examples.rationale: Past workshop activity is followed by a request for the recipient to deliver the schedules. The dispatcher makes no delivery commitment.
examples.text: The workshop completed the winding trials yesterday. Would you send the updated winding schedules to the heritage tram depot?

evidence: We logged the heritage tram motor readings yesterday
please check the depot address, and we intend to send the winding schedules tomorrow.
examples.rationale: The only author-owned future delivery is expressed as an intention. Neither the past work nor the request turns it into an assurance.
examples.text: We logged the heritage tram motor readings yesterday; please check the depot address, and we intend to send the winding schedules tomorrow.

evidence: Tomorrow at noon, our dispatch team will be handing over the heritage tram winding schedules.
Please bring the depot register.
examples.rationale: Scheduled future-progressive delivery by the author's team is firm. The subsequent request is not stated as a condition of that handover.
examples.text: Tomorrow at noon, our dispatch team will be handing over the heritage tram winding schedules. The workshop has completed the motor checks. Please bring the depot register.
